title: Higher derivatives of an interval average
statement: Let $eta>0$, let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $psi:bbrtobbr$ be $m$ times continuously differentiable. For the interval average $S_etapsi(x)=eta^{-1}int_0^eta psi(x+t),dt$, its $(m+1)$st derivative at every $xinbbr$ is $((psi^{(m)}(x+eta)-psi^{(m)}(x))/eta)$.
hypotheses_covered: Real interval length η is positive
ψ is m times continuously differentiable
replaced: For $\eta>0$ and a real function $\psi$, write $S_\eta\psi(x)=\eta^{-1}\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt$. If $m\ge0$ is an integer and $\psi\in C^m(\mathbb R)$, then $(S_\eta\psi)^{(m+1)}(x)=(\psi^{(m)}(x+\eta)-\psi^{(m)}(x))/\eta$ for every real $x$.
